fixes.explanation: Storehouses are where Joseph stored the grain (Genesis 41:48), so it's a fair guess. But the grain is what the people are buying. The money goes somewhere else. Genesis 47:14 says Joseph "…brought it into Pharaoh’s palace." Grain in the storehouses, money in the palace.

Magicians, I see where you got that! They showed up when Pharaoh needed his dream explained (Genesis 41:8), so they're a name you'd remember. But they're not in this scene, friend. Genesis 47:22 says Joseph "…did not acquire the priests’ portion of the land…" No hat, no rabbit, just priests holding on to their land.

True, baker! Pharaoh was already supplying the priests, and the text ties that straight to their land. It says their land "…had been given to them by Pharaoh. They ate the rations that Pharaoh supplied; so they did not sell their land." (Genesis 47:22) Everybody else showed up with empty pockets, and the priests were already covered. The reason is sitting right there in the verse.

False, friend! Joseph "…established a law that a fifth of the produce belongs to Pharaoh, and it is in effect in the land of Egypt to this day." (Genesis 47:26) Nothing in that verse ties the law to the famine ending. That's a law with staying power, like a subscription you forgot to cancel. And the verse adds one more thing: only the priests' land does not belong to Pharaoh.
